open_questions: Depth swings from non-detection in sector 41 to ~2500 ppm in sector 15 within same SPOC 2-min product, not a calibration offset.
Transit depths inconsistent (p_consistent 4.71e-206 with negative depths) despite centroid on-target.
Large phase-curve amplitude (0.4595 of depth) indicates spot modulation – are transits spot-crossings or detrending artefacts?
dossier.public_summary: The dip is centred on the target star with a flat bottom and no secondary eclipse, which would be planet-like, but the depth changes dramatically between sectors and between individual transits, with some non-detections and a large light-curve modulation at the same period. Together the variability best explains the signal as spot-driven dips on this K-dwarf rather than a steady 2.4 Earth-radius planet, while awaiting ground-based follow-up to test stability.

reasons.why: Difference imaging puts the dip on the target, not a background blend, with no NEB able to cause it.
